extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), employers, and policy stakeholders (commenters to the NPRM)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed regulatory criteria for designing, operating, and reviewing registered apprenticeship programs (including pre-apprenticeship and youth apprenticeship), aligning program elements with quality metrics, data reporting, equity, and workplace protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and track success through Equity Indices
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACA recommended that OA 'measure and track success through Equity Indices showing the representation of new, active, and completing apprentices from each underserved demographic group in the context of local area, industry, education/skills, and wages/promotions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Equity Indices to show representation across new, active, and completing apprentices; contextualize by local area, industry, education/skills, and wages/promotions to assess equity outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public, disaggregated apprentice demographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACA recommended that OA 'make apprentice demographic data, disaggregated by race, ethnicity, and sex, and separately for each State and for each standard occupation code, public on a dashboard site.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish demographic data by race, ethnicity, sex, state, and occupation code on a public dashboard to increase transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define apprenticeship / pre-apprenticeship / youth apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACA recommended that the Department 'Define `apprenticeship,' `pre-apprenticeship,' and `youth apprenticeship' to ensure programs align with quality metrics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear definitions so programs can be evaluated consistently against quality metrics and registration standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in quality workforce readiness and pre-apprenticeship programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACA recommended that 'Federal and State agencies should invest in quality workforce readiness and pre-apprenticeship programs' and that the Department encourage employers and registered apprenticeship programs to uplift pre-apprenticeship (e.g., provide conditional offers of registered apprenticeship employment or interviews upon completion of pre-apprenticeship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support and fund pre-apprenticeship programs; link completion to conditional employment offers or interviews to improve transition into registered apprenticeship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools and resources for integrating pre-apprenticeship into education
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to include (1) tools for school counselors and teachers to integrate pre-apprenticeship into curricula and offer students advice on career pathways; (2) resources to connect employers, schools, students, and parents to achieve greater buy-in; and (3) retooling of Apprenticeship.gov to educate public and highlight opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide toolkits for educators, resources for stakeholder connection, and public-facing site improvements to promote uptake and understanding of apprenticeship pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent SAA planning and data reporting via State Apprenticeship Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Department discussion of proposal to make SAA planning and data reporting more consistent through implementation of State Apprenticeship Plans (proposed § 29.27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require or encourage standardized State Apprenticeship Plans to harmonize planning and reporting across SAAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum program duration practice (2,000 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a matter of current administrative practice, OA has ordinarily not registered standards of apprenticeship that have included fewer than 2,000 hours of on-the-job training; current regulations (29 CFR 29.4) do not regard occupations with fewer than 2,000 hours as suitable for apprenticeship training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 2,000 hours as an ordinary minimum benchmark for OJT suitability; recognize that this is administrative practice rather than an absolute statutory limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow reduced minimum duration for advanced standing / prior learning
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed minimum 2,000-hour requirement could be reduced on a case-by-case basis where an apprentice is granted advanced standing, receives credit for prior learning or previously acquired skills/experience, completes registered CTE apprenticeship/pre-apprenticeship, or makes accelerated progress in acquiring occupational competencies (see proposed § 29.8(a)(20)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit individualized reductions to duration when justified by documented prior learning, credit, or accelerated competency acquisition; require appropriate documentation and program approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency attainment and OJT time standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended principle: 'Competency must be obtained under any of these three models; include standards around time in on-the-job training to ensure proficiency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in competency-based models, require standards that tie competency attainment to sufficient OJT time to assure proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect formal, representative data on program and apprentice needs
rubrics_metrics.description: ACA recommended that DOL should gather new data on registered apprenticeship programs' and apprentices' needs through formal, representative surveys, including understanding barriers to completion and long-term career pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement representative surveys to identify barriers to completion, support needs, and career trajectories; use findings to inform policy and program improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggers for more frequent program reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances that may trigger more frequent reviews include a program's reported outcomes consistently falling short of expectations or requirements, and whether serious, unaddressed complaints related to the program, recognized as legitimate by reviewers, consistently arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor program outcomes and complaint patterns; escalate review frequency when persistent underperformance or unresolved legitimate complaints are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align duration reductions with ILO guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.8(a)(20) aligns with ILO Conclusion 10(h), which advises Member States to establish apprenticeship standards that describe 'the extent to which the expected duration of the apprenticeship may be reduced on the basis of prior learning or progress made during the apprenticeship.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When permitting duration reductions, explicitly document the basis and limits consistent with international guidance (prior learning/progress).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent and eliminate discrimination, violence, harassment, and exploitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.8(a)(23) and (24) are consistent with ILO Conclusion 22, advising Member States to take effective measures to prevent and eliminate any discrimination, violence and harassment and exploitation against apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require program measures and safeguards (policies, reporting mechanisms, training) to prevent discrimination, harassment, violence, and exploitation of apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and progressive remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal is aligned with ILO Conclusion 16(a), recommending apprentices 'receive adequate remuneration . . . which may be increased at different stages of the apprenticeship to reflect the progressive acquisition of occupational competencies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set remuneration structures that increase across apprenticeship stages to reflect skill acquisition; consider referencing journeyworker wage percentages or other benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: State examples for final wage-step minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples from Florida Administrative Code and Delaware Administrative Code that utilize minimum standards of 75% and 85% of the established journeyworker wage for the final wage step of the apprenticeship term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider adopting or referencing percentage-of-journeyworker-wage thresholds for final wage step (e.g., 75%–85%) when setting program wage progression policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on apprentice-to-journeyworker ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: ETA, OA Circular No. 2021-02 provides 'Guidelines for Reviewing Apprentice to Journeyworker Ratio Requests.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow OA Circular guidance when reviewing ratio requests; ensure ratios are justified, documented, and consistent with safety and training needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update standards and guidance for new and emerging technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: ACA recommended 'Update and enhance standards and guidance to reflect new and emerging technologies (including any updates to existing or emerging Standards Builder boilerplates/templates).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly revise boilerplates, templates, and guidance to account for changes in technology and evolving industry practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop system for occupational training standards lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: ACA recommended DOL 'develop a plan and the necessary infrastructure to move toward a system for developing, classifying, and updating occupational training standards in [registered apprenticeship].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create infrastructure and processes for continuous development, classification, and updating of occupational training standards to keep curricula current and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed guidance and toolkits for stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: ACA recommended providing detailed guidance so State-level or employer/sponsor-level stakeholders know exactly where to go and what to do to register a program, obtain answers to questions, pursue funding opportunities, and whether there are templates or other guidance to get them started; leverage existing tools like Standards Builder and the Apprenticeship Playbook and develop additional requirement guides as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accessible, step-by-step resources (templates, Playbook, Standards Builder) and supplementary requirement guides to streamline program registration and operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerate deployment in growing industries while ensuring curricula responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: ACA recommended accelerating registered apprenticeship deployment in growing industries and sectors, while ensuring curricula are responsive to industry needs, and templates and requirements are compatible with and flexible for different kinds of jobs and industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target incentives and intermediary contracts to growing sectors; design curricula/templates that are industry-responsive yet flexible across job types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage inclusion of mentorship in programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouraging the inclusion of mentorships in registered apprenticeship programs aligns with ILO Conclusion 25(o).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate structured mentoring components to support apprentices' development and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with education systems for credit and pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: ACA recommendations include coordinating with ED and education institutions to promote provision of academic credit for apprenticeship training or tuition reimbursement and to enhance high school-level apprenticeships with credit given for direct entry into formal registered apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish articulation agreements or credit policies with educational institutions to recognize apprenticeship training for academic credit or tuition support and facilitate transitions from high school apprenticeships to registered programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive services alignment and practitioner guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: References to the Department's approach to supportive services and ETA TEN No. 12-21 'Practitioners Guide to Supportive Services' and relevant WIOA regulations (20 CFR 680.900) on what are supportive services for adults and dislocated workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide or coordinate supportive services per WIOA guidance (transportation, childcare, etc.) to remove barriers to participation and completion; follow practitioner guidance on implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of National Guidelines when no National Occupational Standards exist
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department clarifies that programs can still use National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards if there is not an established set of National Occupational Standards for the subject occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no occupational-specific national standards exist, apply National Guidelines as acceptable baseline standards for registration and program content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather and leverage data and analytics (OA Data and Statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations to OA 'Data and Statistics' and other data sources (O*NET, BLS, etc.) emphasize use of labor and program data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use publicly available data sources and OA analytics to inform program design, occupational selection, and to benchmark outcomes and labor market alignment.
